proposals.relationship: Lawrence invokes Charles Taylor’s interpretive social science to defend hermeneutic readings of personal testimony and socially constructed intersubjective meanings.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2022 reply, paragraph beginning “My defence there, and here” and note 35, explicitly anchors this defense in Taylor’s “Interpretation and the Sciences of Man,” cited in the Rabinow–Sullivan edited reader (1987), 33–81. Lawrence distinguishes reconstructing possible historical subjectivities from statistically representative samples, acknowledges lost interviews and insists on source criticism. This is a particular conceptual resource, not an endorsement of all Taylor’s work or an original Taylor reading. The 1987 manifestation is not asserted as the essay’s first publication; editor credit is separate. The exact printed page for this passage was not independently collated; the verified locator is the original publisher HTML paragraph and note.
primary_locators: Original publisher HTML of On Historians’ Re-Use of Social-Science Archives (2022), paragraph beginning “My defence there, and here,” note 35; preceding lost-fieldnotes qualification. Printed passage page not independently collated.

proposals.relationship: Feldman and Lawrence place Speaking for the People alongside Eley’s A Crooked Line as attempts to connect social structures and discourse.
proposals.evidence_note: Joint 2011 introduction, 8 and note 25, explicitly identifies Lawrence’s 1998 book and says Eley’s 2005 book adopts a similar position on the interconnection of structure and discourse. David Feldman’s equal coauthorship is retained. This is the authors’ particular methodological comparison, not an asserted causal influence, identical arguments, personal collaboration between Eley and Lawrence or a new reading of either complete book. Their account also recognizes the gains of cultural history rather than rejecting it wholesale.
primary_locators: Joint Feldman–Lawrence Introduction (2011), 8, note 25, within publisher excerpt 1–10
